_comment: Player params estimated from video alone (python -m measure.player estimate; see CLAUDE.md 'Player (session s6)'). Inputs were not logged: 'pushing' = speed rising or flat near its plateau. Meters at the PLACEHOLDER scale (rink_length 60 m, 0.06568 m/px); multiply by the real/placeholder scale ratio once it is measured. Only names listed here change; everything else stays in params.json.

player_max_speed.note: top speed: the one flat plateau held >= 0.25 s (rotstick_04: 180 px/s for ~1 s, dead flat, so likely a hard cap). n = 1 run; rotstick_01 peaked at 144 px/s without reaching a plateau. 180.3 px/s at 0.06568 m/px (PLACEHOLDER scale). From events rotstick_04.

player_accel.note: acceleration from rest: median linear ramp (10-90% of each run's own plateau) of the normal starts; the two near-instant 'burst' starts (wall_08, rotstick_04, ~1400-1600 px/s^2) are excluded as dash candidates. The wall-clip starts are short taps (plateau ~35 px/s), so this is the ramp rate, not a time-to-top-speed fit. 241.3 px/s^2 at 0.06568 m/px (PLACEHOLDER scale). From events wall_01, wall_03, wall_05, wall_06, wall_09, wall_10, rotstick_01.

player_ice_drag.note: deceleration when the speed falls to rest, from the stop distance (v0^2 / 2d). Without an input log a release cannot be told from active braking (opposite key): the stops take 0.07-0.25 s, and where the speed held flat for a while before the stop no decay was visible, so the real coasting drag may be much lower and this a brake. 396.1 px/s^2 at 0.06568 m/px (PLACEHOLDER scale). From events wall_01, wall_03, wall_05, wall_06, wall_09, wall_10, rotstick_01, rotstick_04.
